Marissa / Rishi — initial triage:
- No deploys to the hosted runtime or model catalog between 17:30–19:00 PT. CI/CD shows last rollout at 11:02 PT.
- Autoscale events: there was an aggressive up-scale starting 17:58 PT for dedicated pools (customers on Dedicated), but hosted pools show a transient backlog spike on the websocket frontend at 18:07 PT.
- Key observation: batch size distribution for streaming connections shifted to more small batches (1-2 tokens) between 18:05–18:25 PT (likely due to a change in client behavior from Voyager’s side — more frequent partial-edit sends). That reduces batching efficiency and increases per-token cost and latency.
- No infra OOMs or GPU driver errors.

I’ve pulled request traces and attached a p95/p99 chart for the window. Also flagged the websocket worker queue length increased ~3x at the top of the spike.

Attachments: slo-p95-p99-chart-20261007.png

I recommend: temporarily enable our aggressive batching fallback for Voyager’s project to coalesce small writes (we can toggle at project config). This should bring p99 down quickly while we continue deeper profiling.

Dev
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: chat throughput degradation tonight

Got the traces — adding context from the runtime side: 
- KV cache hit ratio dropped ~12% for Voyager’s project during the spike window; per-request KV miss causes longer decode paths and extra memory touch.
- Observed several requests that hit our fallback model variant (rdx-13b-v1-quant) under higher concurrency; the variant has slightly higher per-token latency under short-burst workloads.
- Websocket frontends showed increased connection churn (clients reconnecting) which amplifies tail.

Action taken: enabled the conservative batching override for Voyager at 17:50 PT (before the main spike) in a quick test, but we fully rolled the aggressive batching override at 17:55 PT after confirming no regression in correctness. Post-toggle, p99 improved within ~8–10 minutes in our synthetic tests.

I’m continuing to profile model-side decode hotspots and will check whether we need a targeted rollback of model variant routing for their tenancy.

Rishi
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Anita —

Thanks for the quick flag and for sending logs. We triaged the window you called out: 18:05–18:40 PT on 2026-10-07. Summary and next steps: 

What we saw
- Root-candidate contributors: a shift to many small client writes (reduced batching efficiency), increased connection churn (reconnects), and a temporary drop in KV cache hit ratio for your tenancy. These together drove higher per-request decode time and queueing on our websocket frontend which manifested as the p95/p99 uplift and ~7% timeouts you observed.

Immediate mitigation (already applied)
- Aggressive batching override enabled for Voyager at ~17:55 PT (rolled fully 17:55–18:00 PT). In synthetic verification and live sampling we saw p99 improve within 8–12 minutes after the override.

What we’re doing next (timeline)
- Short (today): Rishi/Dev will check model-variant routing and KV tune to avoid falls to the quant variant for short-burst workloads (ETA 6 hours).
- Medium (48–72 hrs): collaborate with Voyager Eng on client telemetry to reduce chattiness (we can propose small client-side debounce) and instrument more detailed event traces.
- Exec briefing (tomorrow): we’ll deliver a one-pager (timeline, root-candidates, impact, proposed credits) and offer a 30m call — propose 10:00 PT tomorrow.

We’re committed to making this right. If you want the one-time credit offer to be considered ahead of the call, we can provisionally hold a credit pending a short impact window from your side.

Attachments: remediation-playbook-v1.pdf

Please let us know whether 10:00 PT tomorrow works for your team and whether you’d like us to include our CTO/ops lead on the call.

Best,
